title: The Exaltation of the Cross (14 September)
hookLine: the cross found in Jerusalem, honored as a tree of life

lines: A THIRD TREE ON A HILL.
cards: The Bible begins in a garden with a tree in the middle of it, the tree of life, and ends in a city where the tree of life grows again, beside a river.
In between, Christians say, there's a third tree: two beams of rough wood on a hill outside Jerusalem. Good Friday is the day the Church grieves at that tree.
But there's a second day for the cross, in September, with no grief in it at all. The priest wears red, the Gloria is sung, and the Church calls the cross by a startling name.

teach.b: The story begins with Helena, the mother of the emperor Constantine. Tradition says that late in her life she traveled to Jerusalem, had the hill of Calvary excavated, and found the wood of the cross there.
Historians can't confirm the details, and the Church tells it as tradition.

teach.h: A CHURCH OVER CALVARY; LIFTED HIGH.
teach.b: Constantine built a great church over the site of the tomb and Calvary. Tradition keeps its dedication on the thirteenth of September; on the fourteenth, the cross was lifted up and shown to the people.

That's what exaltation means: lifting high. Centuries later, the story goes, a Persian army carried the relic off and the emperor Heraclius brought it back, and that homecoming became part of the feast too.
The Gospel for the day is John three, where Jesus compares himself to the bronze serpent Moses raised in the desert, which healed anyone who looked at it.
In the Douay-Rheims: "as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of man be lifted up." The thing that should mean death is lifted up as healing.
A Latin hymn by the poet Venantius Fortunatus, still sung on Good Friday, has the line "Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbor una nobilis": faithful cross, the one noble tree among all trees.

teach.h: SO MUST THE SON OF MAN BE LIFTED UP.
teach.b: In the hymn, the instrument of execution becomes the tree of life. That reversal is today's feast.

how: Catholics celebrate the feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross on 14 September with red vestments and the Gloria; the Gospel is John 3:13–17, and some parishes hold a veneration of a relic or crucifix.

games.q: you're an Israelite in the desert, bitten by a serpent. Moses has raised a bronze serpent on a pole. what heals you?
o: looking at the serpent lifted up.
games.why: whoever looked at it lived. Jesus uses it in John three: so must the Son of man be lifted up.

practice: Trace the sign of the cross on yourself as slowly as you can, forehead, chest, left shoulder, right shoulder, as if your hand were lifting something heavy and good; if you don't make the sign, trace a cross in the air or on the table with one finger.
Then think of one thing in your life that once felt like a dead end and became a way through.

wordCard.voice: Crux fidelis. Latin for faithful cross: the line where Venantius Fortunatus calls it the one noble tree among all trees. Today's word.
